name: cost
description:
The arithmetic, as an editorial price sheet: head centred, the illustration full-width with the statement riding on it, the comparison as two cards facing each other across the pair's rule, the highlighted rate leading the claim, and a ticker of what the price buys.

The comparison is carried by what each card IS — the old cost dimmed and struck like a disabled control, the offer on the success tint (marine on it measures 12.15:1, the most headroom either card has, which is the right way round for the one you are meant to read). Both figures are set at the SAME size: a comparison whose two figures differ in scale has already answered itself.

Every colour here is a measurement. The overlay's parens take `secondary-edge` (3.87:1 on the scrim, where paradise reads 2.50). The closing rate sits on `secondary-strong` (4.61:1 under cream) because it is running text and paradise itself is 3.93. The offer card's ink never softens: 78% marine measured 3.21:1 on the unit line and axe was right.

base.$description: Hugging on purpose: the section unit already declares the container everything in here measures with `cqi`, and a second container between them would change what every clamp reads.

story.$description: The head is centred with everything else in the section, and it opens with room: an eyebrow butted against the band above it reads as a continuation of that band rather than the start of this one.

overlay.$description: The statement rides ON the picture, on the bottom THIRD as a band — not a caption sized by its own padding. A marine scrim rather than a drop shadow: the illustration's sky is sunflower and its water pale, so no single tone carries type unaided. The gradient ABOVE fades the scrim up so the summit stays untouched.

&::before.background: linear-gradient(to top, color-mix(in oklab, var(--color-marine) 88%, transparent), transparent)

& .paren.$description: One step lighter on the same ramp: paradise measures 2.50:1 on this scrim, `secondary-edge` 3.87 — a colour that carries on one ground does not carry on every ground.

price.$description: Composes `pair pair--rule-none`. The gap the cascade was actually resolving to — two rules set it once, and the later 16px won; the pair unit reads `--gap`.

was.$description: The cost being declined, styled the way this system styles something no longer available: muted ground, quiet ink, the whole card carrying the dimming rather than the number alone. Ranged toward the rule — two blocks both ranged left is a list; ranged toward each other, a comparison.

& .cost-panel-label, & .cost-now-unit, &.$description: FULL marine on the tinted field. Softening ink on a coloured field is the same error as tinting it on cream: 78% marine measured 3.21:1 on the unit and 4.39 on the note, both short of the 4.5 body text needs.

was-value.$description: The page's own gesture, third appearance: the hero strikes a sentence, the shift a script, this a salary. CSS, not `<s>` — SAFE_TAGS admits no `s`.

closing.$description: The verdict the whole comparison exists to deliver, set like one: the page's ink, a step up in size, tracked caps.

closing-rate.$description: The rate leads, highlighted — it is the thing being claimed. `secondary-strong`, not paradise: cream on paradise is 3.93:1 and this is a running snippet, so 4.5 applies; the darkened step is 4.61 and holds at any size.

does.$description: The ticker: short facts edge to edge, separated by marks. Static — motion here would be decoration that has to be switched off again for anyone who asked for less of it.

a11y.note: The heading keeps its id as the section's `aria-labelledby` target. The struck salary is real text — a reader hears both figures — and the strike is reinforced by the copy naming which cost is being declined. The overlay statement is a `<figcaption>`, so the picture and its claim announce as one figure.
